meta.title: Who wrote "Manic Monday"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: It was The Bangles' breakthrough hit — but they didn't write it. "Manic Monday" was written by Prince, under the pseudonym Christopher. Who wrote it, and why his name isn't on it.
meta.ogDescription: Not a Bangles original composition. Prince wrote it, credited as 'Christopher', and gave it away — then blocked it from No. 1 with his own single.

writing.label: Written by Prince — not The Bangles
writing.sourceLine: ‘Manic Monday’ was The Bangles’ first big hit, and like most bands they’re assumed to have written their own breakthrough. They didn’t: it was written by Prince, credited on the release under the pseudonym Christopher, who handed it to the band and then kept it off No. 1 with a single of his own.
writing.definitiveVersion: The Bangles’ 1986 single — the only version released in Prince’s lifetime.
trail: The song is credited to Christopher, a pseudonym Prince used at the time; his authorship is confirmed by his own catalogue and by The Bangles, who have described being given the song.
Prince wrote it around 1984, originally intended for the side project Apollonia 6, before it went to The Bangles.

The detail that gives the authorship away: in April 1986 ‘Manic Monday’ was held at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 by the No. 1 single — Prince’s own ‘Kiss’. He wrote the No. 2 and performed the No. 1 in the same week.

misattribution.heading: The attribution problem
misattribution.intro: The song is so associated with The Bangles that the writing credit is assumed to be theirs. It isn’t — and the real writer is one of the most recognisable names in music, which is what makes the correction land.

items.why: It was their debut hit and the song most identified with them, so the composition is assumed to be theirs.

misattribution.truthLine: Written by Prince under the name ‘Christopher’, and recorded by The Bangles — who performed it, but did not write it.

context.heading: Why Prince gave it away
lead: Prince spent the mid-1980s writing far more than he could release under his own name, placing songs with other acts — sometimes under pseudonyms like ‘Christopher’ or ‘Alexander Nevermind’. ‘Manic Monday’ was one of these.

That the writer was Prince, rather than an anonymous staff songwriter, is exactly why the credit surprises people: a band writing its own hit is unremarkable, but a global superstar quietly authoring someone else’s is a story.
context.pull: Prince held No. 1 and No. 2 at once — one as the artist, one as the writer.

authors.name: Prince
authors.bio: Among the most prolific songwriters of his era, Prince wrote and produced hits for many other artists, often uncredited or under pseudonyms. He was credited as ‘Christopher’ on ‘Manic Monday’.

authors.name: The Bangles
authors.bio: Their 1986 recording of ‘Manic Monday’ was their commercial breakthrough. The band wrote much of their own material — but not this song.

schema.faqAnswer: "Manic Monday" was written by Prince, credited under the pseudonym Christopher. It was recorded by The Bangles, whose 1986 version was a US and UK No. 2 hit — but the band did not write the song.
